newsitem.title: GERMANY: kohl slams SPD, vows to continue tax fight-paper.
newsitem.headline: kohl slams SPD, vows to continue tax fight-paper.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, in an interview with a German newspaper, sharply criticised opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and said their refusal to agree tax reforms would cost them in elections next year.

The SPD leadership, in an "unscrupulous" grab for power, had blocked the reforms in hopes that a worsened economy would sweep them into office in the vote scheduled for November 1998, Kohl told the Welt am Sonntag.

"The SPD leadership was not ready for an agreement from the beginning," Kohl said in an interview due to appear on Sunday. "The SPD leadership was much more interested in a worsening of the situation. The coalition will lay the responsibility for that on them and will profit from it in the 1998 election."

SPD chief Oskar Lafontaine has said his party wants to win the election and then pass its own tax reforms. The SPD, saying Kohl's package favoured wealthy taxpayers, used its majority in the upper house to block the measures in parliamentary discussions last week.
Nevertheless, Kohl said the government would try again to push through 30 billion marks in tax reductions. "We will propose a motion for a second mediation attempt," he said.
In another interview, Finance Minister Theo Waigel also told Welt am Sonntag the coalition was determined to get a tax deal through despite the SPD blockade.
"We will turn up the pressure on Lafontaine so much that the SPD rank and file themselves will ask what is (he) trying to do," Waigel said.
